research_question: After a statistically extreme multi-bar return (z-scored against its own trailing volatility), does price tend to reverse over a comparable following window - a classical short-term-reversal/liquidity-provision-correction mechanism, deliberately distinct from the old rejected Bollinger+RSI+trend-efficiency mean-reversion baseline and from Hypothesis 1's own unconditional lag-1 autocorrelation finding (attributed to bid-ask-bounce noise)?

why_this_is_not_a_retune.old_baseline: mean_reversion_signals_4h.py: Bollinger(20,2std) band + RSI(14,30/70) + Kaufman trend-efficiency filter - a 'stretched from a short-term range, in a non-trending market' story. Tried at 1H/4H/daily, all REJECTED (near-breakeven at best).
why_this_is_not_a_retune.this_hypothesis: a z-scored MULTI-BAR RETURN extreme (no bands, no RSI, no trend filter) - a 'sharp, fast move overreacted and partially reverses' story, mechanistically distinct.
why_this_is_not_a_retune.distinction_from_H1_baseline_A: H1's Baseline A found GBP_USD's unconditional lag-1 M15 autocorrelation was weakly negative (r=-0.030, p<0.0001) but attributed this to generic bid-ask-bounce microstructure noise, not a real economic effect, since it appeared symmetrically regardless of which instrument 'led'. This test uses 4H (far coarser, much less bid-ask-bounce-prone) and CONDITIONS on a genuine multi-bar statistical extreme (|z|>=2), not the unconditional bar-to-bar autocorrelation H1 already found and explained away.

scope.instruments: PORTFOLIO_SYMBOLS - EUR_USD, GBP_USD, USD_JPY, XAU_USD (same scope as the old 4H mean-reversion baseline being re-tested)

pre_registered_protocol.zscore_normalization: trigger return divided by its own trailing 60-bar (~10 trading days) standard deviation - fixed, standard normalization, not tuned
pre_registered_protocol.forward_window: the FOLLOWING 3-bar (12h) cumulative log return - same horizon as the trigger window
pre_registered_protocol.no_lookahead: z-score and classification use only data up to and including the trigger bar's own close; forward window is strictly after
pre_registered_protocol.mechanical_simulation_design_not_run: direction counter to the extreme (short after extreme-up, long after extreme-down), entry at next bar's Open with realistic Ask/Bid fill + SLIPPAGE_ATR_FRACTION=0.02xATR (reused from backtest_engine.py), structural stop beyond the extreme run's own multi-bar High/Low + 0.1xATR buffer (reused style from V1/V2/H4/Candidate 2), fixed 1:1 R:R target, 70/30 chronological train/test split matching run_backtest.py's TRAIN_FRACTION - designed but NEVER EXECUTED because Part 1's statistical premise was rejected first

pre_committed_rejection_criteria.stage_1_statistical_premise: REJECTED if forward return is not significantly reversal-signed in BOTH directions (extreme-up group not significantly negative, OR extreme-down group not significantly positive) - no mechanical trade simulation run if triggered
pre_committed_rejection_criteria.stage_2_would_have_applied_if_stage_1_su: REJECTED if mechanical trade simulation's profit factor does not clear the NEW standing bar (>1.3) in BOTH train AND test, or if train/test PF diverges beyond the new standing tolerance (test PF < 0.65x train PF)

extreme_up.note: correctly signed (negative) but not significant at combined level

extreme_down.note: WRONG-signed (should be positive for reversal) and not significant

EUR_USD.note: the one cell with a genuinely significant, correctly-signed reversal - but only one of eight instrument x direction combinations tested

USD_JPY.note: extreme-up group WRONG-signed (continuation, not reversal), though not significant

results_part1_statistical_premise.interpretation: No stable, consistent reversal pattern across instruments or years. The one nominally-significant, correctly-signed result (EUR_USD extreme-up) is one cell out of eight instrument x direction combinations tested - with that many comparisons, one nominally-significant hit is close to what chance alone predicts, and it wasn't paired with a significant reversal on the same instrument's other side or replicated in any other instrument.

results_part2_mechanical_simulation: NOT RUN - stopped per the pre-committed stage-1 rejection rule before any trade simulation, cost modeling, or evaluation against the new standing criteria (PF>=1.3, trade count, IS/OOS similarity, concentration, multi-regime) was performed.
verdict: REJECTED at the statistical-premise stage. Neither pre-committed condition was cleared: the extreme-down group is wrong-signed and not significant; the extreme-up group is correctly signed but only borderline (p=0.057, not significant) at the combined level. Results are inconsistent across both instruments (2 of 4 show a wrong-signed continuation on at least one side) and years (only 2020 significant, 2 of 5 years wrong-signed). This differs in KIND from Candidates 1-3 (which also failed on premise) and from Hypothesis 4 (which survived the premise and failed on execution cost) - this is a clean premise-stage rejection, killed at the cheapest possible point in the process, before any mechanical trade simulation or cost modeling was attempted.
does_not_proceed_to: Mechanical trade simulation, signals module build, tests, or entry point - none were written. Mean-reversion as a signal type, retested fresh (not reusing the old baseline's Bollinger/RSI construction), still does not hold up in this project's data.
